title: Playing guitar-and-horn duets with Lonnie Johnson in Raceland
summary: Punch says he and Lonnie played as boys near Raceland for about three years, doing blues and old numbers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Yeah, I think so. Let me ask you something. You and Lonnie work where now? R-A-C-E-L-E-N-D. Raceland? Yeah. Where's that at? It's about 40 miles from there. Louisiana. Yeah. You played together for how long? I'd say about three years. We were young kids. Just the two of you? Yes, just the two of you. We didn't have no band. Where would you play? Well, them old numbers. Remember them old tunes I'd sing to you, Dick?

Old numbers. Beautiful doll. And Take Your Hands Away. And Blues. A whole lot of blues, you know. A lot of blues. Oh, he was a fine guitar, man. He's the guitar on this, I think. Yeah, but the only thing. Did you ever hear of Blind Willie Dunn? Yeah, I heard him. Was he Ed Lang? I don't know.
